title: Unified hydrodynamics for density and spin supersolids
authors: Ashwath N. Madhusudan, Au-Chen Lee, P. B. Blakie, R. N. Bisset
abstract: Two-component supersolids can exhibit in-phase or out-of-phase component density modulations, corresponding to density and spin supersolids, respectively. We formulate a general hydrodynamic theory for the collective dynamics of multicomponent supersolids, guided by their broken symmetries and conservation laws. We benchmark it against microscopic calculations for a binary dipolar condensate confined to an infinite tube, finding quantitative agreement for the sound speeds of all three Goldstone branches throughout the density- and spin-supersolid regions. The resulting relations link collective-mode measurements to elastic coefficients and superfluid fractions.
summary: This paper develops a unified hydrodynamic theory for two-component supersolids, modeling systems like dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates. By deriving equations of motion from symmetry and conservation laws, the authors predict the collective excitation spectrum, including sound speeds. The theory is rigorously benchmarked against microscopic calculations, confirming its quantitative accuracy across the spin- and density-supersolid phases.
main_problem: To formulate a general hydrodynamic theory describing the collective dynamics of multicomponent supersolids, which exhibit both density and spin modulations.
main_result: The hydrodynamic predictions for sound speeds quantitatively agree with microscopic Bogoliubov–de Gennes calculations across the entire phase diagram, confirming the theory's validity.
method: The theory is derived from symmetry and conservation laws, leading to Euler-Lagrange equations whose normal-mode solutions are used to calculate sound speeds and elastic coefficients.
model_or_system: The system is a binary dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (or quantum gas mixture) confined to 1D, exhibiting supersolid phases characterized by density and spin modulations.
key_observables: Sound speeds of the three Goldstone branches ($c_{s}, c_{d\pm}$), superfluid fraction ($f_{sf}$), and elastic coefficients ($\alpha_{dho dho}$, $\alpha_{sho sho}$).
important_parameters: Relative dipole moment ($\mu_{m2}/\mu_{m1}$), interspecies scattering length ($a_{12}$), and the component imbalance.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the long-wavelength limit ($\omega = cq$) and utilizes the symmetric-mixture approximation for the quantum-fluctuation energy density ($\epsilon_{QF}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing spin- and density-supersolid regions, and provide hydrodynamic predictions for sound and elasticity along specific cuts (balanced and imbalanced).
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the Lagrangian and Euler-Lagrange equations for the hydrodynamic fields, analyzes the resulting dynamical matrix in different limits (imbalanced, balanced spin, symmetric density), and compares the resulting dispersion relations against microscopic BdG calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unified theoretical framework connecting macroscopic hydrodynamic measurements (like sound speed) directly to microscopic parameters (like dipolar interactions and superfluid fractions) in complex quantum matter states.

Phase diagram showing spin- (green) and density- supersolid (blue) ground state regions as a function of relative dipole moment (horizontal axis) and interspecies scattering length (vertical axis).
